name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.OneDependencyDeclarationPerStatement
displayName: Use one dependency declaration per statement
description: The Gradle Groovy DSL accepts multiple coordinates in a single configuration call (e.g. `implementation 'a:b:1.0', 'c:d:2.0'`), but the Kotlin DSL does not. Gradle's best practices recommend declaring a single dependency per statement; see the [Gradle dependency best practices](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html). This recipe splits multi-coordinate Groovy DSL configuration calls into one call per coordinate. Run this as a cleanup pass before other dependency-aware recipes (e.g. `UpgradeDependencyVersion`, `ChangeDependency`, `RemoveDependency`): those recipes use the `GradleDependency` trait, which only inspects the first argument of a configuration call. Coordinates in later positions are invisible to them until this recipe reshapes the source into one declaration per statement.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.RemoveExplicitKotlinStdlibDependency
displayName: Remove explicit Kotlin standard library dependency
description: The Kotlin Gradle plugin adds the version of `kotlin-stdlib` that matches itself, so declaring the dependency explicitly is redundant and can pin a version that disagrees with the plugin. Removes `org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib` and its `-jdk7`, `-jdk8` and `-common` variants, written either as coordinates or with the Kotlin DSL `kotlin("stdlib")` helper, but only from a project that applies a Kotlin plugin — without one the standard library is an ordinary dependency the project needs, and removing it would stop the build compiling. Only `implementation` declarations are removed, because that is the one configuration the Kotlin plugin contributes the standard library to: a declaration on `api` is consumer-visible through the published compile scope, and one on a configuration of the project's own has nothing putting it back. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html#dont_depend_on_kotlin_stdlib).

description: Remove a dependency declaration whose configuration already receives the same dependency from a configuration it extends. `testImplementation` extends `implementation`, and in `java-library` `implementation` extends `api`, so declaring one coordinate on both reaches nothing the wider declaration did not already reach â€” the second line only has to be kept in step with the first. description: Replace `project.getLogger()` in a `Plugin` with a `private static final Logger` obtained from `Logging.getLogger(TheClass.class)`. description: Replace a top-level `apply plugin:` statement with an entry in the `plugins` block, which Gradle can resolve before configuring the build and which tooling can read without running it. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.settings.MoveRepositoriesToSettings
displayName: Declare dependency repositories in the settings file
description: Move a build script's top-level `repositories` block into `dependencyResolutionManagement` in the settings file, so the build has one place that says where dependencies come from and a project cannot quietly resolve from somewhere the rest of the build does not. Deliberately narrow, because the risk is all in the cases it declines: a build with more than one project is left alone, since hoisting one project's repositories applies them to every project and can change which repository a coordinate resolves from; `buildscript` repositories resolve the build's own classpath, which `dependencyResolutionManagement` does not serve; `publishing` repositories are where artifacts go rather than where dependencies come from; and a block inside `allprojects` or `subprojects` is multi-project configuration whatever the build looks like today. A settings file that already declares `dependencyResolutionManagement` is left for a person to merge. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html#set_up_repositories_in_settings).

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.RemoveNonReproducibleArchiveSettings
displayName: Remove archive settings that defeat reproducible builds
description: Remove `preserveFileTimestamps = true` and `reproducibleFileOrder = false` from archive tasks, in either DSL spelling, so the archive takes Gradle's own default instead. The reproducible values written explicitly are left alone, since someone who wrote them agrees with the default and said so deliberately. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_security.html#builds_should_be_reproducible).

description: Pin the SHA-256 checksum of the Gradle distribution the wrapper already downloads, by adding `distributionSha256Sum` to `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` when it is absent.
